::: {.justify style="margin: 50px 0;"}

I am contributing to the development of metamaterial-based tip-transforming catheters at Nimble Surgical.
Previously, I was a Faculty Research Assistant in the Intelligent Machines and Materials Lab, part of the Collaborative Robotics and Intelligent Systems (CoRIS) Institute at Oregon State University.
I developed hardware for integrating flexible sensors for augmenting human-supervised underwater grasping. Prior to this, I built and characterized electrically-driven soft grippers and a robot arm,
and improved the performance of Pneu-Net actuators.

My work sits at the intersection of mechanical engineering, robotics, materials, and computation to some extent.
I design the system, fabricate it, characterize it, then feed what I learned back into the design.

Outside of work, I am a virtual pilot and hobbyist photographer.

Read more about my work on the [research](research.html) page.

:::
